function.name: healthMDDModel
function.description: Analyze the probability of health and MDD in the EEG data between [start, end] seconds. Minimum segment length is 5 seconds. If the interval is longer than 5 seconds, the function splits it into consecutive 5-second segments and returns a list of probabilities for each segment. Probabilities can be averaged to get a subject-level assessment.

returns.description: List of dictionaries with segment duration and probability of Health and MDD

function.name: normalAbnormalModel
function.description: Analyze the probability of pathological normality and abnormality in the entire EEG record.

returns.description: Probability of pathological normality and abnormality

function.name: reflectData
function.description: This function should only be called when no effective information can be obtained from other tools. Directly extract a 1-second segment of raw data.

name.description: List of channel names to extract, e.g., ['FP1-F7', 'F7-T3']

returns.description: A dictionary with channel names as keys and corresponding EEG data arrays as values

function.name: eyemMuscleModel_OneSecond
function.description: Use this tool to classify the type of artifact (eye movement or muscle) in EEG signals within a specific short time window (typically 1 second). It should be called only when artifacts have already been detected or suspected. Input channels should be in bipolar format (e.g., 'FP1-F7' or 'F7-T3'), and the analysis duration must be short (1–10 seconds). The tool returns, for each second, the probability that the signal belongs to 'Eye movement' or 'Muscle artifact'.

name.description: List of EEG channel pairs to analyze (e.g., ['FP1-F7', 'F7-T3']). If the user mentions a single channel like 'FP1–F7', wrap it in a list.

start.description: Start time in seconds. Extract this from user query, e.g., 'from 10s'.

end.description: End time in seconds. Extract this from user query, e.g., 'to 11s'. The interval should typically be 1 second.

returns.description: Each element in the list corresponds to one second of analysis. Each dictionary includes the time duration and, for each channel, the probabilities of 'Eye movement' and 'Muscle artifact'.

function.name: seizureArtiBckgModel_OneSecond
function.description: Use this tool to analyze EEG signals and estimate the probability that a given channel segment (typically 1 second) belongs to one of three classes: 'Background', 'Artifact', or 'Seizure'. This is a fine-grained classifier suitable for second-level EEG inspection. Use it when the user asks questions like 'What type of activity is between 20 and 21 seconds in FP1-F7?' or 'Is this second more likely seizure or artifact?'.

name.description: List of EEG channel pairs to analyze (e.g., ['FP1-F7', 'C3-P3']). Supports reversed order like 'F7-FP1'.

end.description: End time in seconds (e.g., 21). The duration must not exceed 10 seconds; 1 second is recommended.

returns.description: A list where each item corresponds to one second of analyzed data. Each dictionary contains the time window and, for each channel, the probabilities of 'Background', 'Artifact', and 'Seizure'.

function.name: seizureNormalModel_OneSecond
function.description: Compute the probability of seizure vs. non-seizure activity for each channel within a specified time window. The function processes the data in 1-second segments, and returns probabilities for each segment and each channel. The time interval between start and end must not exceed 10 seconds.

end.description: End time in seconds. Maximum allowed interval: 10 seconds.

returns.description: A list of dictionaries, one per 1-second segment. Each dictionary contains the segment duration and the seizure/non-seizure probabilities for each channel.

function.name: sleepStageModel
function.description: Predict 5-class sleep stages for a given EEG segment. The input segment should be at least 30 seconds long. This tool divides the segment into non-overlapping 30-second epochs, and returns the probabilityfor each of the 5 sleep stages ('W','N1','N2','N3','R') for each epoch.

start.description: Start time of the EEG segment in seconds.

end.description: End time of the EEG segment in seconds.

returns.description: A list of dictionaries, one per predicted segment. Each dictionary contains 'duration' as the time window string, and 'Prob' which is a dictionary of sleep stage probabilities, e.g., {'W': 0.1, 'N1': 0.2, 'N2': 0.5, 'N3': 0.1, 'R': 0.1}.

function.name: slowSeizBckgModel_TenSeconds
function.description: The probability that the data analyzed between [start, end] seconds contains slow waves, epilepsy, and background activity.

returns.description: A list of dictionaries. Each dictionary represents 10 seconds of analyzed data.

function.name: compute_amplitude
function.description: need end - start <= 60. Compute amplitude features (mean absolute, RMS, peak values) of specified EEG channels in a given time window.

name.description: List of channel names to analyze, e.g., ['FP1-F7', 'F7-T3']

returns.description: A dictionary where keys are channel names and values are dictionaries of amplitude features including: mean_abs, rms, max_val, min_val

function.name: compute_psd
function.description: need end - start <= 60. Compute power spectral density (PSD) of specified EEG channels in a given time window and integrate by frequency bands.

name.description: List of channel names to analyze, e.g., ['FP1-F7', 'F7-T3']

returns.description: A dictionary where keys are channel names and values are dictionaries of power values for each frequency band, unit: V²

function.name: compute_symmetry
function.description: need end - start <= 60. Calculate the Pearson correlation coefficient between specified left and right channel pairs within a given time window to assess EEG signal symmetry.

channel_pairs.description: List of left-right channel pairs, e.g., ['FP1-F7', 'FP2-F8')].

returns.description: A dictionary with channel pairs as keys and Pearson correlation coefficients, Structural Similarity Index as values.
